speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in light of sudden incidences of disruption of Saudi Arabia's oil supply and the potential risk of such incidences happening (a) what is the impact on Singapore's economy; (b) how will this affect the prices of our electricity supply to consumers; and (c) how will this affect prices of petrol for motor vehicles.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry with regard to the recent attack on Saudi Arabia's oil production facilities (a) what has been the impact on Singapore's oil imports from Saudi Arabia; (b) whether oil prices are expected to rise and impact inflation as a result of these attacks and their aftermath; and (c) what is being done to manage the risk of rising oil prices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First, our oil supply remained sufficient throughout the period of outage.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, this incident is a useful reminder to us about the importance of energy security, especially given ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is particularly pertinent to Singapore as we import almost all our energy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Government adopts several strategies to secure our energy supply and keep energy prices competitive.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We encourage our oil and gas traders to import from multiple sources, while our oil refineries leverage their global resources and supply chains, as well as the wider oil trading ecosystem, to ensure a continuous supply of crude oil if there is a disruption in any supply source.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Second, while electricity prices in Singapore cannot be insulated from global energy price movements, Singaporeans can enjoy competitive electricity prices because we continue to promote competition in our electricity market.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Open Electricity Market (OEM) is one such initiative to give households and small businesses more choices of retailers to buy electricity from.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As the Senior Minister of State had noticed, when oil prices abroad rise, it is usually symmetrical.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When oil prices rise, prices at the petrol kiosks rise as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But my question is related to the Senior Minister of State's first point, in terms of our strategy to search for alternative sources of energy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can MTI share what are our plans in terms of alternative energy sources for Singapore, going forward?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My concern is that the incidence of such things happening in the Middle East may intensify or increase, particularly from drone attacks and possibly from geopolitical tensions arising out of the Middle East as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Our traders have sourced for oil not just from the Middle East, but places in the US as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, the diversification is a robust strategy to make sure that we are not threatened by a single source, where there may be problems that occur with that supply.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In terms of electricity, the generation comes largely from gas, whether it is piped or liquefied natural gas (LNG).

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, in terms of electricity supply, that ensures our needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is something that we can be well assured about.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Of course, over time, more households may come on.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I do not have the updated number as of this moment, but we do see that there are fluctuations from month to month.
